newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ashanti in Ghana gold mines deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ashanti in Ghana gold mines deal.

text.p: Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd said on Friday it has acquired full ownership of two gold mines in Ghana and rights to a third after agreement with the Ghana government.

Ashanti said it will transfer US$15.5 million, mostly in new Ashanti shares, to the government for a 10 percent stake in Ghanian-Australian Gold Fields Ltd, whose principal holding is the Iduapriem gold mine, and a 10 percent interest in Cluff Resources Ghana Ltd, whose main asset is the Ayanfuri mine.

The Africa-based miner, which is listed on several exchanges including the Australian Stock Exchange, also acquired rights to take up the 10 percent it does not own already own in the Bibiani project, with a resource of over two million ounces.
The Iduapriem mine produced 115,298 ounces of gold in the 12 months ended June 30, 1996 and had net assets of US$25.3 million, Ashanti said.
Before tax profit for the year to June 30, 1996 was US$2 million.
Anyufuri produced 49,225 ounces of gold in the year ended September 30, Ashanti said.
Before-tax profit for the year ended December 31, 1996 was US$3 million, it said.
Ashanti's interest in Bibiani is held through its two wholly-owned subsidiaries, Ashanti Goldfields (Bibiani) Ltd and International Gold Resources Corp, both of which were acquired in June 1996.
Evaluation work has delineated resources of about 20 million tonnes grading 2.9 grammes a tonne of non-refractory surface material, Ashanti said.
Of the total transfer price, US$13.9 will be settled by the issue of new Ashanti shares an the rest in cash, Ashanti said.
The Ghana government currently holds l8.6 percent of the issued share capital of Ashanti.
On completion of the transfers the government will hold 19.4 percent of the issued ordinary share capital of Ashanti, the company said.
Except in limited circumstances or with the consent of Ashanti, the government has agreed not to dispose of the new Ashanti shares for 12 months, the company said.
Ashanti merged with Australia-based Golden Shamrock Mines Ltd in October last year to further its West African gold resource base. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
